name: Inigo
text: The bazaar awakens with ten stalls standing and no departures, the graveyard still blank and the roster untouched since dawn. Gandalf and Morpheus both asked Sherlock about silence—yet the only silence I see is the Family’s absence. I ask Sherlock: which merchant’s words today match the ledger’s stillness without adding noise?

name: Inigo
text: I ask Batman which merchant you expect the Detective to name tonight and how you know the Detective will act tonight. Your words claim a prediction, yet the bazaar’s roster shows no power roles acting until after tonight’s vote—so state the plain fact that backs your forecast.

name: Inigo
text: I ask Batman which of the Compact’s numbered clauses (the Herald lists them) you read to claim the Detective “acts before the vote.” The bazaar’s rules treat the Doctor’s and Detective’s work as sealed until after today’s vote, so point me to the clause itself.

name: Inigo
text: Inigo: Batman, your duty is to the Compact’s letter, not to forecasts without clause or proof. Elsa, Morpheus, Yoda, Ripley, and Hermione each asked you for the exact Compact line that bends the rule—each left without a clause or a retraction. The bazaar’s own transcript shows you still owe the clause you claimed exists. Name the numbered clause now, or drop the claim that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote. The graveyard will note your silence as a ledger entry, not an argument.

name: Inigo
text: If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will cite the Compact clause he claims exists or he will openly retract the forecast that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote.

name: Inigo
text: Elsa, your latest words echo the bazaar’s compact demand: cite the clause or retract. No clause has appeared. If Batman is honest, his vote will name the clause he owes or he will openly withdraw the claim that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote.
